\subsection{Discretization and Anti-Windup}
\label{sec:antiwindup}
Because the integrator Youla-H plants in $G_{CYH}$ is an \emph{exact} pole at $s=0$, the controller separates uniquely into an integrator and a strictly stable remainder,
\begin{equation} \label{eq:split}
G_{CYH}(s) = \frac{k_I}{s} + R(s), \qquad k_I = K_{YH}\frac{\prod_{i} z_i}{\prod_{p_j\neq 0} p_j}.
\end{equation}
No such split exists for $G_{CH}$, whose integral action is buried in the slow pole pair of Equation \ref{eq:Gch}. The split makes the digital realization well posed: the integrator is discretized by the trapezoidal rule as an explicit scalar state, and $R(s)$ is balance-truncated (which requires a stable system) and discretized by Tustin's method. The explicit integrator state also admits the standard PI anti-windup schemes, back-calculation or conditional integration, directly.

Figure \ref{fig:YH-AW-18} applies this to the drivetrain system with a $5$\,m/s step and an illustrative limit $|T_e|\le 0.1$\,N$\cdot$m, chosen to rail the actuator for about $2$\,s. With a clamp alone, $G_{CH}$ and $G_{CYH}$ alike wind up, overshooting $71\%$ with a $10$\,s relay-like recovery. Back-calculating into the integrator alone releases the rail but leaves an $18\%$ standing error: here $k_I = 1.8\times10^{-3}$ while $R(0) = 42$, so the lag states of $R$ hold most of the low-frequency gain and wind up on their own. Conditioning the full state with the general Hanus law \citep{hanus1987conditioning}, $x_{k+1} = A_d x_k + B_d e_k + L\,(u_{\mathrm{sat},k}-u_k)$, leaves the linear controller unchanged off the clamp and de-winds every state on it: $1.3\%$ overshoot, settled $2.2$\,s after the step. $L$ is pole-placed rather than the self-conditioned $B_d/D_d$, because Tustin's method gives Equation \ref{eq:split} a $(z+1)$ numerator factor that puts a saturated-mode eigenvalue at exactly $z=-1$. The conditioned counterpart of the integrator remains a slow positive-real mode and must be left in place, since it carries the integrator's memory.

    \includegraphics[width=1\linewidth]{Figures/YH-AW-18.pdf}
    \caption{Saturated step response of the drivetrain system (reference in light gray): clamp only, integrator-only back-calculation on the realization of Equation \ref{eq:split}, and full-state conditioning.}
    \label{fig:YH-AW-18}
\end{figure}
